Key Takeaways

Needham kept its Buy rating and $300 target on Reddit on Oct. 9, 92% above the Oct. 8 close, after the stock lost 40% from its January high.

Slower guided growth, choppy search traffic and doubts about renewing its AI data deal with Google have weighed on the shares this year.

Earnings estimates are rising, and the stock trades at 18.3x forward earnings, near its one-year low and well below its 27.7x average.

Needham's target implies about 35x forward earnings, so the call is plausible but stretched.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) has lost 40% since its Jan. 13 closing high, and Needham hasn't budged. On Oct. 9, analyst Laura Martin kept her Buy rating and $300 target, 92% above the stock's $156.47 close on Oct. 8.

Three hits since January

On Jan. 27, Cleveland Research analyst Ross Walthall warned of slower growth in 2026. The stock fell 9% that day.

On July 30, Reddit reported second-quarter revenue up 61% to $805 million, but management guided to 47% to 49% growth for the third quarter. CEO Steve Huffman said "Search referrals were choppy in the quarter and traffic was more volatile later in the quarter."

In mid-September, Wells Fargo said it sees a lower chance that Reddit's AI data deal with Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ) renews.

Needham still sees $300

Martin's case leans on AI: she has argued that Reddit's human-written content has no comparable substitute at its scale, and in June she said its data deals with Alphabet and OpenAI could renew at higher fees.

Does $300 add up?

The rest of the Street is more cautious: the consensus target has slid from $252 in early February to $214, near its low for the year.

Reddit (RDDT): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

Still, nobody's capitulating. The lowest target rose from $110 to $130 over the year, and Buy ratings went from 13 to 16.

Earnings estimates point the same way. Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from $4.54 in 2025 to $11.85 in 2028.

Reddit (RDDT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)

And they've risen since the July report: Yahoo Finance's tally of 29 analysts has lifted its 2027 EPS estimate to $7.07 from $6.47 90 days ago. (It counts earnings differently than TIKR does.)

Meanwhile, the stock is cheap against its own history: it trades at 18.3x forward earnings as of Oct. 8, close to its one-year low and well under its 27.7x average.

Reddit (RDDT): forward (NTM) P/E, last year (TIKR)

Needham's $300 works out to about 35x the $8.55 a share analysts expect over the next twelve months. That's well above the past year's average, though far short of January's 48.6x peak.

Cheap, but $300 is a reach

The risk is traffic. If search referrals keep sliding and the Alphabet deal doesn't renew on better terms, that 47% to 49% guide could be just the start of the slowdown.

3 Overrated Stocks We Think Twice About

Great things are happening to the stocks in this article. They're all outperforming the market over the last month because of positive catalysts such as a new product line, constructive news flow, or even a loyal Reddit fanbase.

But not every company with momentum is a long-term winner, and plenty of investors have lost money betting on short-term fads. On that note, here are three stocks that are likely overheated and some you should look into instead.

FormFactor (FORM)

One-Month Return: +19.1%

With customers across the foundry and fabless markets, FormFactor (NASDAQ:FORM) is a US-based provider of test and measurement technologies for semiconductors.

Why Does FORM Worry Us?

Sales trends were unexciting over the last five years as its 3.8% annual growth was below the typical semiconductor company

High input costs result in an inferior gross margin of 42.8% that must be offset through higher volumes

Lacking free cash flow generation means it has few chances to reinvest for growth, repurchase shares, or distribute capital

FormFactor is trading at $136.03 per share, or 40.5x forward P/E. To fully understand why you should be careful with FORM, check out our full research report (it's free).

Fortrea (FTRE)

One-Month Return: +21.3%

Spun off from Labcorp in 2023 to focus exclusively on clinical research services, Fortrea (NASDAQ:FTRE) is a contract research organization that helps pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies develop and bring their products to market through clinical trials and support services.

Why Do We Pass on FTRE?

Products and services are facing significant end-market challenges during this cycle as sales have declined by 3% annually over the last five years

Negative returns on capital show that some of its growth strategies have backfired, and its falling returns suggest its earlier profit pools are drying up

Waning returns on capital from an already weak starting point displays the inefficacy of management's past and current investment decisions

Fortrea's stock price of $20.36 implies a valuation ratio of 21.7x forward P/E. Dive into our free research report to see why there are better opportunities than FTRE.

Amneal (AMRX)

One-Month Return: +12.6%

Founded in 2002 and growing into one of America's largest generic drug producers, Amneal Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:AMRX) develops, manufactures, and distributes generic medicines, specialty branded drugs, biosimilars, and injectable products for the U.S. healthcare market.

3:35pm: Small cap wrap

U.S. Global Investors (NASDAQ:GROW) CEO Frank Holmes argues that gold miners remain undervalued despite September's gold selloff, pointing to central bank buying, ETF inflows and demand in China and India alongside improving cash flow and earnings.

Alvopetro Energy Ltd (TSX-V:ALV, OTC:ALVOF, FRA:A6Y0) has received positive analyst feedback on its entry into Brazil's Tucano Basin, which brokerages view as a low-cost opportunity to establish a third growth platform by leveraging its existing operating and gas marketing expertise.

EnWave Corp (TSX-V:ENW, OTC:NWVCF, FRA:E4U) has signed a royalty-bearing commercial licence with Ashland Dehydrated Foods, which purchased two 10kW Radiant Energy Vacuum machines for use in food and pet food manufacturing.

Montero Mining and Exploration Ltd (TSX-V:MON, OTC:MXTRF) has raised C$1.5 million through a non-brokered private placement to fund drilling at its Elvira Gold Project in Chile.

2:30pm: Market movers

Delta Air Lines Inc (NYSE:DAL) cut its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast to $5.10 to $5.60 per share from $6.50 to $7.50 as higher jet fuel costs pressured margins, following quarterly earnings that missed analyst expectations.

AT&T Inc (NYSE:T, XETRA:SOBA), T-Mobile US Inc (NASDAQ:TMUS, XETRA:TM5) and Verizon Communications Inc (NYSE:VZ, XETRA:BAC) stocks moved lower after news that SpaceX Corp (NASDAQ:SPCX) is expanding Starlink into mobile services.

Aritzia Inc (TSX:ATZ) reported a 204.2% increase in second-quarter net income to C$201.7 million, supported by tariff refunds, 44.1% revenue growth and stronger comparable sales.

Reddit Inc (NYSE:RDDT) is gaining a larger share of digital advertising budgets, with Horizon Media reporting annual growth of 20% to 25% in its share of client spending over the past three years.

Penguin Solutions received a Buy rating and $100 price target from Bank of America, which cited demand for memory and AI infrastructure.

MTY Food Group raised its quarterly dividend by 35% to C$0.50 per share despite lower third-quarter net income and weaker comparable restaurant sales.

Lumentum Holdings said strong demand for optical and laser components used in AI data centres has effectively booked its production capacity through early 2029, sending shares up more than 4%.

Humana (NYSE:HUM) shares surged nearly 15% after the insurer improved its 2027 Medicare Advantage quality ratings, with about 95% of members enrolled in plans rated at least four stars.

1:00pm: iPhone 18 demand concerns

Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL, XETRA:APC) (Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL, XETRA:APC), Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL, XETRA:APC)) faces growing iPhone 18 Pro demand concerns as delivery waits shorten, with UBS retaining a 'neutral' rating and $296 price target.
